result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers give a clear headline, three consistently structured stacked cards with full-width buttons, a native details-based FAQ and a logical section order, all within comfortable mobile margins. A makes its FAQ more distinct by using a flat ruled list instead of cards, but its in-flow 'Most popular' tag and dark featured card slightly break the shared card structure. B keeps its cards more uniform by placing the badge absolutely and listing plans in increasing hours, but its FAQ uses cards that look a lot like the plans. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B's first screen is clearer: a top bar, a headline that names the action and a line of context, so visitors see at once that they are choosing a course. Its cards put labelled hours and price on one row, and its FAQ is a flat ruled list that clearly differs from the plan cards. A is clean and well built, but its FAQ uses cards much like the plans, it puts hours and price on separate lines, and its headings skip from h1 to h3.
